title: Advance Wars: Dual Strike
subtitle: Another front opens
summary: Advance Wars: Dual Strike is Intelligent Systems' turn-based strategy game for Nintendo DS. The Allied Nations confront Black Hole in Omega Land, where the enemy is draining energy from the landscape. Armies of infantry, tanks, aircraft and ships contest a grid of properties and terrain. body: Advance Wars: Dual Strike is Intelligent Systems' turn-based strategy game for Nintendo DS. The Allied Nations confront Black Hole in Omega Land, where the enemy is draining energy from the landscape. Armies of infantry, tanks, aircraft and ships contest a grid of properties and terrain. Captured factories supply reinforcements, while headquarters offer a direct target. The colourful presentation makes each unit easy to distinguish, but the campaign still asks the player to balance local victories against the money and positions needed for the next turn.

An army can be assigned two commanding officers, with the player switching between their different strengths. CO powers alter the conditions of a turn, while a Tag Power allows both commanders to use their Super CO powers in succession. That can give one army a devastating period of uninterrupted action. Preparing the opportunity matters as much as activating it: units need to be close enough to exploit the advantage. The additional commander changes planning before the special move rather than merely supplying another attack animation.

The DS allows selected missions to split the conflict between two fronts. Attention can move from the main battlefield to another engagement above it, while maps and unit information make use of the extra screen elsewhere. Weather, fog of war and terrain continue to affect how safely a force can advance. The second display extends an established strategy language instead of replacing it. A player who recognises the old units still has to learn how activity on one part of the operation can support another.
